title: Reported Speech Quiz 3
description: Report questions with statement order, and choose between if, whether and a question word.
instructions: Use the standard rule: the reporting verb is in the past and the situation is over, unless a question says otherwise.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Report this: 'Where do you live?' she asked me.
options: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I lived.
She asked me where I do live.
questions.explanation: A reported question uses statement order and no do: where I lived. Watch out: the word order goes back to subject then verb.

questions.question: 'Do you like tea?' Tom asked Ann. Tom asked Ann ___
options: if she liked tea.
did she like tea.
if did she like tea.
that she liked tea.
questions.explanation: A yes / no question becomes if + statement: if she liked tea. Watch out: you becomes she and did is dropped.

questions.question: 'What are you doing?' she asked him. → She asked him what {{1}} {{2}} doing.
questions.explanation: The report keeps statement order: what he was doing. Watch out: you becomes he, and are becomes was.

questions.question: 'Have you finished?' he asked me. → He asked me {{1}} I had finished.
questions.explanation: A yes / no question needs if or whether. Watch out: that is not used for questions.

questions.question: 'She asked where was he' is correct.
questions.explanation: A reported question uses statement order: She asked where he was. Watch out: the question order does not follow into a report.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He asked me what time was it.
He asked me what time is it.
He asked me what time it is?
He asked me what time it was.
questions.explanation: The report keeps statement order and moves back one step: what time it was. Watch out: neither was it nor is it fits.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported question.

rows.given: 'Where is the bank?' he asked her. He asked her ___.
'Do you speak French?' he asked her. He asked her ___.
'Has she called?' he asked her. He asked her ___.
'What are you doing?' he asked her. He asked her ___.
'Will you come?' he asked her. He asked her ___.

questions.explanation: Statement order, one step back, and no question mark. Watch out: will becomes would, and has called becomes had called.

questions.question: Match each direct question with its report.
right: He asked if it was open.
He asked if I knew him.
questions.explanation: Each report has statement order and moves the verb back. Watch out: do you know becomes if I knew, with no did.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The reporting clause, then the question word, then the subject and the verb. Watch out: I lived has statement order.

questions.question: Report this: 'Can you help me?' she asked him.
options: She asked him if he can help her.
She asked him if he could help her.
She asked him could he help her.
She asked him if could he help her.
questions.explanation: A yes / no question needs if, statement order and could. Watch out: you becomes he and me becomes her.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: She asked me did I know him.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me what was my name.
They asked if I was ready.
She asked whether he had arrived.
questions.explanation: The correct reports have no inversion and no extra do. Watch out: did I and was my name keep the question order.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: She asked me where did I put the keys.
accepted: She asked me where I put the keys.
She asked me where I put the keys
She asked me where I had put the keys.
She asked me where I had put the keys
questions.explanation: The report uses statement order, with no did: where I put the keys, or where I had put the keys. Watch out: both tenses are possible after the backshift.
